title: Beyond the D <= N^{0.172} wall for thin matrix products
credit: Majdoddin, Thin matrix products up to D ≤ N^0.172 and lossless reductions for 3SUM, Exact Triangle and APSP, arXiv:2610.17420 (Oct 2026); building on Alman–Vassilevska Williams arXiv:2610.06783.
premise_risks: arXiv:2610.06783 (Alman–Vassilevska Williams, Oct 2026 preprint): assumes the thin-product subroutine and the subquadratic 3SUM / subcubic APSP refutation.
arXiv:2610.17420 (Majdoddin, Oct 2026 preprint): assumes ε* ≥ ln4/(5 ln5) and that ⟨34,2,35⟩ is open.
arXiv:2610.42012 (Chan–Itakura–Ma–Yu, Nov 2026 preprint): makes the stated 3SUM payoff stale (3SUM already O(n^1.965)).
plain: AVW's core subroutine computes requested entries of XY (N x D times D x N, D <= N^{eps}) in N^2/D^{c} operations; Majdoddin extends the regime to eps < ln4/(5 ln5) ~ 0.17227, matching Coppersmith's 1982 exponent for the same tensor. Either (a) extend the thin-product theorem to some eps > 0.17227 (e.g. via a different base identity, or settle Majdoddin's open thin product <34,2,35>), giving 3SUM/APSP exponents below 1.9945 / 2.9945; or (b) prove that every partial-product-tensor/Coppersmith-style scheme is limited to eps <= 0.17227.
math: Call ε good if there is γ > 0 such that for every constant K some deterministic word-RAM algorithm, given 1 ≤ D ≤ N^ε, X ∈ ℤ^{N×D}, Y ∈ ℤ^{D×N} with |entries| ≤ N^K and a list of at most N²/√D index pairs, outputs those entries of XY in O(N²/D^γ) time. Let ε* = sup of good ε. Is ε* > ln4/(5 ln5)? (Barrier version (b) is a separate question.)
